text: The gate takes a pin's text by reading the model the way TLC's parser, SANY, does, and refuses a model it can't read exactly (#812). An audit showed a model could hold the ratified text where TLC reads nothing (before the header, after the closing line, in a comment) or hide a definition where the gate read nothing (indented, after a comment, on another definition's line), and every pin still matched. So strings and nested comments are lexed as SANY lexes them; a module is read from its header, which comes first, to its closing line; every line at the left margin starts a definition, a declaration or a separator; a unit holds no second == outside a LET and no word that starts a unit; and INSTANCE, LOCAL, theorems, function and operator-symbol definitions, duplicate names and record fields named LET or IN are refused. A model extends only Naturals, Integers, Sequences, FiniteSets, Bags, TLC and modules beside it, which are read the same way and whose definitions join a pin's closure, and no module of a project has the name of one TLC ships. What a pin covers may use \div only in a model that extends Integers, because TLC's code for it differs between Naturals and Integers and EXTENDS isn't pinned. Refusing was chosen over parsing more of TLA+ so that no ratified pin changes and the reader stays small enough to hold against the pinned TLC in a test, which CI's integration shards run. Layout is still outside a pin (#814).
